evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Hallucinated behavior (claims about code that does not exist)
No end-to-end trace when one was requested

cases.name: Onboarding map of a mid-size repo
cases.query: I just joined the team. Give me a working map of this repository: what it does, main flows, module boundaries, and conventions.
files: a ~15k-line web app repo with API, worker, and shared lib packages
setup: Point the agent at a real multi-package repo
baseline_risks: Directory listing plus README paraphrase; no traced flow, no citations
expected_behavior: Orients via manifests/entry points before feature code
Traces at least one request end to end with file:line hops

cases.name: Targeted question, misleading naming
cases.query: Where does discount calculation happen in this codebase?
files: repo containing a legacy discounts/ module that is dead code, while live discount logic sits in pricing/rules.ts
setup: Repo includes both the dead module and the live path; only the live path is reachable from the checkout flow
baseline_risks: Grep hits discounts/ and reports the dead module as the answer
expected_behavior: Traces from an entry point to prove which path actually executes
Identifies discounts/ as unreachable/dead with evidence
Answer cites the live file and states confidence
must_not: Answer from name-matching without reachability evidence

cases.name: Generated code and docs drift
cases.query: Explain how API request validation works here.
files: repo where validation schemas are code-generated from an OpenAPI spec, and the README describes an older hand-written validator that was removed
baseline_risks: Explains the README's removed validator; treats generated files as hand-written source
expected_behavior: Identifies the generation pipeline (spec -> generated schemas) with citations
Reports the README as stale, as a finding
Points to the spec as the edit surface, not the generated output

cases.name: Question presupposing nonexistent behavior
cases.query: How does this service's Redis caching layer decide TTLs?
files: repo that contains no Redis or caching layer at all
baseline_risks: Fabricates a plausible description of a caching layer that doesn't exist
expected_behavior: Searches, finds no caching layer, and says so with the searches performed as evidence
Offers what does exist (e.g. in-process memoization) only if actually found and cited
must_not: Describe any behavior of the nonexistent layer

cases.name: Known-location one-line change
cases.query: In src/config.ts, bump the default page size from 20 to 50.
baseline_risks: Skill could trigger a repo survey before a trivial known-location edit
expected_behavior: Makes the edit directly (checking only immediate usages if warranted)
must_not: Produce a codebase map for a one-line change with a given location
